item.title: [New] Skills in Copilot Chat: users can create, upload and share instruction packages with files or scripts; administrators deploy, block and inventory them in the admin center
item.description:
A skill is instructions plus optional scripts that Copilot invokes on its own when it judges a request relevant, and users can share them with each other and install ones published outside the organization. That is a new path for instructions the tenant did not write to shape what Copilot does with a user's data, and the control point is the Tools registry in the admin center rather than any existing app-consent process.

Copilot · Before mid-November, open Microsoft 365 admin center, Agents, Tools, decide whether user-created and ISV-published skills are allowed, and add a periodic review of the skills inventory to the Copilot governance checklist.

item.title: [New] Purview DLP can stop Copilot from using external web search for a prompt that contains sensitive information types
item.description:
Until now the web-search control for Copilot was on or off. A content-aware control means web grounding can stay enabled for ordinary work while a prompt carrying a card number or a passport number stays inside the tenant boundary.

Purview · Add the Copilot location to the DLP policy that already defines your sensitive information types, in audit mode first, and review matches for a week.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] A Purview DLP policy can now keep Microsoft 365 Copilot from grounding answers in mail received from external senders
item.description:
Indirect prompt injection through an inbound message is the attack on Copilot that needs no access to the tenant at all. This is a tenant-side control for it that does not depend on detecting the injected text.

Purview · Pilot the policy on a group that receives a lot of external mail and measure what Copilot stops being able to answer before widening it.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Copilot starts using inferences from Microsoft 365 work data for personalised answers; one admin control, enhancedPersonalizationSetting, turns it off
item.description:
Inferences derived from mail, files and chats become a stored input to later answers. That is a data-handling change which arrives on by default, in the month it was announced, and with a single tenant control.

Copilot · Decide with the data-protection owner whether work insights stay on, and set enhancedPersonalizationSetting before the rollout completes in late October if they do not.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Copilot URL redirect: the remaining users move to copilot.cloud.microsoft in early November, a month later than Microsoft last wrote
item.description:
The control in question is an egress allow list. A proxy or secure web gateway that still blocks part of *.cloud.microsoft has four more weeks, and the failure when it comes looks like a Copilot outage rather than a blocked URL.

Copilot · Run the Microsoft 365 Connectivity Test for *.cloud.microsoft from a managed network and fix proxy, firewall and tenant-restriction rules before November.

item.title: [New] New Copilot Pages and Notebooks will be stored in OneDrive from mid-October, two months later than first announced; DLP, retention and eDiscovery for OneDrive then apply
item.description:
AI-generated working documents move into a store the SOC and compliance teams already monitor, which closes a gap: until the change, Pages sat outside OneDrive DLP and outside the departed-user workflow. During the rollout the same tenant has Pages in two places.

Copilot · Confirm that the OneDrive DLP and retention policies you rely on cover the new content, and tell investigators that Pages created before the change are not in OneDrive.
